Class Hl7v2SpanDecorator

java.lang.Object
org.apache.camel.telemetry.decorators.AbstractSpanDecorator
org.openehealth.ipf.platform.camel.ihe.core.IpfSpanDecorator
org.openehealth.ipf.platform.camel.ihe.hl7v2.Hl7v2SpanDecorator
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.apache.camel.telemetry.SpanDecorator
Direct Known Subclasses:
MllpDispatchSpanDecorator, MllpSpanDecorator, PamIti30SpanDecorator, PamIti31SpanDecorator, PdqIti21SpanDecorator, PdqIti22SpanDecorator, PixIti10SpanDecorator, PixIti8SpanDecorator, PixIti9SpanDecorator, XdsIti8SpanDecorator, XpidIti64SpanDecorator
public abstract class Hl7v2SpanDecorator extends IpfSpanDecorator
Base class for the span decorators of the HL7v2 transactions.

Unlike the SOAP and HTTP based transactions, HL7v2 has no transport that could propagate trace context, which is why this is the one family where IPF has to do it: the context travels in a nonstandard segment, see Hl7v2TraceContext.

  • Reading happens here, in getExtractor(Exchange): when camel-telemetry creates the span for an incoming message the body is still the encoded message, which is exactly what can be read without parsing.
  • Writing cannot happen here, because at that moment the outgoing message does not exist yet. The context is therefore handed to ProducerTraceContextInterceptor through an exchange property, and that interceptor writes it into the message it has by then.
Details of the message itself are added once it has been parsed, see afterTracingEvent(Span, Exchange).
Since:
6.0

Christian Ohr
